requirement_text.REQ-364:
Implements REQ-363's design artefact exactly — no new schema decisions here, this requirement is implementation of an already-validated design, matching this project's own CODE-DESIGNER-then-ELIXIR-DEV split for every other schema-bearing feature.

SCOPE: the `Letflow.Help` context module (naming follows this project's existing per-domain-context convention, e.g. `Letflow.Identity`, `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`) exposing: create a draft, update a draft, publish (draft -> live, sets confirmed_at), re-confirm (bumps confirmed_at on an already-live row without changing body — the explicit "I checked this, it's still accurate" action), and read (by screen_id + tenant prefix, or by process_definition_id). Every write path enforces REQ-363's sanitization rule from that design, not a weakened version of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the tenant-facing authoring UI (REQ-365 for platform, a separate future requirement for the tenant admin UI itself — this requirement's acceptance criteria stop at a working, tested context module, callable from IEx/tests, not yet wired to any HTTP route or frontend component). Route/controller wiring, if this project's own API-surface convention wants a separate requirement for it (matching the pattern most REQ-027..030-style definition CRUD work already used), is a natural fast-follow, not bundled here — state explicitly in this requirement's close-out whether a route was added or deliberately deferred, rather than leaving it ambiguous.

task.description: Implement the AST-based markdown sanitizer per CODE-DESIGNER's now-validated req363-help-content-data-model.md section 5.4 (rework 2), replacing the rejected regex-denylist approach in lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex. Verify any edge case the design does not explicitly cover directly against the real earmark_parser dependency rather than trusting the design text, and flag any verified deviation for SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER.
acceptance_criteria: help_content.ex's write-path sanitizer uses EarmarkParser.as_ast/2 and an AST walk per design SS5.4.2, all regex-only sanitization code removed
mix.exs gains earmark_parser as a dependency, citing the governing decision record
mix test test/letflow/help_test.exs and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass, real output quoted
Any verified gap between the design's stated mechanism and the library's real behavior is fixed and explicitly flagged for review, not silently patched

result.summary:
RECONSTRUCTION NOTE: this handoff was originally written live during WF02-REQ364-20260917's security-review saga as ad-hoc, non-schema JSON (informal top-level keys such as req/at/result-as-bare-string instead of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's real schema), the exact anti-pattern this session's own ISS-0692 precedent names. It has been rewritten into full schema conformance by a later ORCH session under §4.1's not_agent_attested mechanism. created_at/started_at/completed_at are all set to the file's own git-introducing-commit timestamp (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%aI --reverse -- <path>`), the best-available real timestamp, NOT the original live dispatch/claim/completion times, which were never recorded in schema-legal fields on disk. All findings, quoted test counts, and verification detail below are migrated verbatim in substance from the original ad-hoc file; nothing was invented or paraphrased away.

Replaced regex sanitization with EarmarkParser.as_ast/2 AST walk per design SS5.4.2. mix.exs gained earmark_parser ~> 1.4, citing decision 0036. help_content.ex: deleted all regex module attributes/helpers, added validate_markdown_safety/2 + walk/1 + raw_html_node?/2 + destination_violation/2 + scheme_letters/1 + decode_numeric_entities/1.

TWO VERIFIED GAPS FOUND IN DESIGN AND FIXED:
1. Raw HTML mixed inline with surrounding text is never tagged verbatim: true by earmark_parser 1.4.46 (only line-starting tags are) -- confirmed directly against the library's own moduledoc and live calls, not trusted from the design text. Added a bounded fallback scan of unparsed plain-text AST leaves for tag-shape patterns, excluding code-node content structurally so SS5.2's fenced-content-is-literal guarantee still holds.
2. Numeric HTML entity references and embedded whitespace/control characters in resolved href/src are NOT decoded/stripped by the library -- fixed by decoding decimal/hex numeric character references then keeping only ASCII a-z letters from the pre-colon portion before scheme comparison.

VERIFICATION: mix test test/letflow/help_test.exs: 47 passed (33 original + 14 new covering all 5 bypass classes plus legitimate-content cases). mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean. mix deps.get resolved earmark_parser 1.4.46 cleanly.

FLAGGED FOR REVIEW: the two verified-gap deviations from the design's stated mechanism need SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER sign-off before TEST-DESIGNER.

issues.description: Two deviations from design SS5.4.2's stated mechanism (inline-mixed raw HTML not tagged verbatim by the real library; numeric entities/whitespace not decoded by the real library) were found and fixed during implementation, not anticipated by the design -- flagged for SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER sign-off rather than silently patched.
